about: The motion library: reusable animations (moves) for any brand. One entry per move. A move is in this file only if it has a working example in the gallery.

reel.does: Plays every move one after another. One file per brand: motion-<brand>.mp4.

families.type: How words and numbers arrive and change.
families.emphasis: Drawing the eye on a product screen.
families.transition: Getting from one scene to the next.
families.capture-pointer: Pointer styles drawn over a product capture (CaptureClip).
families.capture-effect: Click, hover and typing effects on a product capture.
families.capture-camera: Camera moves over a product capture, from tracks.json and hand-set cues.
families.capture-time: Speed ramps, freezes, jumps, rewinds, pins and loops, all through one time map.
families.capture-look: Look presets: one word sets the pointer, click, camera and pace of a capture.
families.capture-staging: Where the screen sits: frames and layouts around a product capture (CaptureShot, staging.tsx).
families.capture-product: Animations on the product, glued to tracked things (CaptureClip's emphasis, emphasis.tsx).
families.capture-sound: Interface sounds placed from a capture's event log (sound.ts, tools/audio/capture_sounds.mjs).
families.capture-transition: Transitions between two captures, or two parts of one, on one film clock (CaptureJoin, transitions.tsx; the plan is joins.ts).
families.capture-relayout: A wide capture re-laid out for 9:16, 1:1 and 4:5, the camera following the action inside the recording; a phone-size take full frame (relayout.ts, CaptureShot in a tall or square frame).
families.caption: Short-form caption styles a brand may choose for 9:16 (decision 6); the fixed caption design stays the default.
families.opener: Hook openers: the first two seconds, made in the engine, a pattern interrupt without anyone else's footage (knowledge/craft/15-hooks.md).
families.shader: Shader backgrounds on Paper Shaders, coloured from the brand, frame-accurate (render with --gl=angle).
families.ugc: Creator-style moves for phone and screen-share films: the comment a film answers, the marks of a screen recording, a sticker reaction (engine/src/kit/ugc/).

moves.name: blur-in
moves.does: Each word of a headline is there, soft, at once; it reaches its place first and comes into focus last.
moves.use_when: Calm films, and headlines that should arrive gently.
moves.avoid_when: Fast or hype passages, and any line that must be read the instant it appears.

props.lines: One or two clauses. The first is in ink, the second in the second colour. Star one word to set it in the accent voice.
props.at: Seconds on the scene clock when the move starts.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: tracking-settle
moves.does: The letters of one line start a little wider apart and close up, from rest, slowing into the brand's own spacing.
moves.use_when: The opening line or the closing line of a film.
moves.avoid_when: Sentences in the middle of a film, and more than one line at a time.

props.at: Seconds on the scene clock when the move starts.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: rotating-word
moves.does: The last word of a line swaps for another inside a box that resizes to fit, while the rest of the line holds still. The words are on one roll: the old one leaves through the top as the new one comes up, and nothing fades.
moves.use_when: One line that is true for several audiences or uses.
moves.avoid_when: More than four words in the rotation, or when the changing word is not the last on the line.

props.lead: The words before the box. Optional.
props.words: Two or more words, shown one at a time.
props.at: Seconds when the line and its first word arrive.
props.every: Seconds each word stays, taken from the voice: about half a second of reading plus the swap.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: number-roll
moves.does: The digits of a number roll to their value in fixed-width figures, the last digit landing last. A number that arrives comes up from empty through a few digits per wheel, blurred while fast; it never spins a full turn and never shows a leading zero.
moves.use_when: Prices, counts and percentages, and a value that updates from an old number to a new one.
moves.avoid_when: Numbers that must be compared with a bar or a ring (use count-with-bar), and an old value that is longer than the new one.

props.at: Seconds when the roll starts. It ends one scene length later.
props.from: The old value, on screen before the roll. Optional. Without it the number arrives rolling.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.prefix: Text before the number, such as a currency sign. Optional.
props.unit: Text after the number at 60% of its size, such as %. Optional.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: type-on
moves.does: Characters appear at a human rhythm: bursts of a few letters, with small pauses at spaces and punctuation.
moves.use_when: Prompts and search fields in product UI.
moves.avoid_when: Film headlines, and long text that nobody needs to watch being typed.

props.at: Seconds when the first key is pressed.
props.over: Seconds the typing takes in all. Optional. A prompt takes 2 to 3 seconds whatever its length.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.caret: Show the caret, a line in the accent colour. Optional; on by default.
props.seed: A number that picks the rhythm. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: swap-word
moves.does: One word rolls out through the top of the line and its replacement rolls in from below, while the rest of the line holds. The two are never printed over each other.
moves.use_when: Before and after in one line.
moves.avoid_when: More than one swap in a line, or when the swapped word is not the last on its line.

props.lead: The words before the swapped word. Optional.
props.from: The old word, in the warm colour.
props.to: The new word, in the accent.
props.swapAt: Seconds when the word is swapped.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: drawn-mark
moves.does: An underline, or a ring drawn as a hand draws one (a little square, a little uneven, its end passing outside its start), is drawn on its child in the accent colour.
moves.use_when: Pointing at one word, number or control without adding text.
moves.avoid_when: With another emphasis on the same beat (a lift, a focus pull), or more than one mark on screen at once.

props.children: The word, number or control to mark.
props.at: Seconds when the mark is drawn: an underline in a quick length, a ring in a base length.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.weight: Thickness of the stroke as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.gap: Space between the child and an underline, as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: focus-pull
moves.does: Everything except the chosen child dims and softens.
moves.use_when: One thing in a group matters for this beat.
moves.avoid_when: More than five things in the group, or with another emphasis on the same beat.

props.children: The group. Each child sits in a box of its own.
props.keep: Which child stays sharp, counting from 0.
props.out: Seconds when focus is given back. Optional.
props.style: CSS that lays the group out. Optional.
props.itemStyle: CSS for each child's box. Optional.

moves.name: lift
moves.does: A card rises off the surface: it grows 2 to 3% and its shadow grows and softens. On a dark page, where a shadow hardly shows, it also catches light along its top edge and rim and a soft glow of the accent spreads under it.
moves.use_when: A selected card or row, on either page.
moves.avoid_when: With another emphasis on the same beat.

props.children: The card. Give it no shadow of its own.
props.out: Seconds when it is set down again. Optional.
props.radius: Corner radius of the card as a percentage of frame height. Optional; the brand's window radius by default.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: stagger
moves.does: The items of a group arrive in order from a source: the left, the centre, or a point.
moves.use_when: Rows, tiles and lists arriving as a result.
moves.avoid_when: Groups of more than about twelve, and a single item.

props.children: The items. Each sits in a box of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the first item arrives.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.from: "left", "centre", or the position (counting from 0) of the item at the point, such as the one the cursor clicked. Optional; left by default.
props.columns: How many items per row, when the group is a grid. Optional.
props.style: CSS that lays the group out. Optional.
props.itemStyle: CSS for each item's box. Optional.

moves.name: count-with-bar
moves.does: A number counts up while its bar grows. The last step of the count lands as the bar comes to rest.
moves.use_when: One number that matters, shown against a whole or a target.
moves.avoid_when: Several numbers at once, and a number with no meaningful maximum (use number-roll).

props.max: The value of a full bar.
props.at: Seconds when the label and the faint track arrive.
props.countAt: Seconds when the count and the bar start. Optional; just after the label by default.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.label: A short label above the number. Optional.
props.unit: Text after the number at 60% of its size. Optional.
props.width: Width as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.size: Type size as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

also_exports.Count: The counting number on its own, for the middle of a ring or beside a line. Props: value, at, from, over, decimals.

moves.name: bar-grow
moves.does: One bar grows from its baseline to its value and slows into place.
moves.use_when: Before against after, or a small chart of up to about six bars, each started a little after the last.
moves.avoid_when: Charts that need a legend, and bars that do not start at zero.

props.share: The bar's value as a share of the full length, 0 to 1.
props.at: Seconds when it starts to grow.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.length: Full length as a percentage of frame height.
props.thickness: Thickness as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.over: How long it grows: a timing token. Optional; base by default.
props.track: Show the full length, faint, before the bar arrives. Optional.
props.emphasis: Paint the bar in the accent: the one bar the chart is about. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: line-draw
moves.does: A line draws itself along a path, and its end mark appears last.
moves.use_when: Change over time as one line, or connecting two things on screen.
moves.avoid_when: Several lines at once, and before the viewer has seen both ends.

props.points: Two or more places the line passes through, in pixels of the frame.
props.at: Seconds when it starts to draw.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.over: How long it draws: a timing token. Optional; scene by default, base or quick for a connector.
props.curve: Draw one smooth curve through the points. Optional.
props.weight: Thickness as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.mark: Show the end mark, a short stroke across the end. Optional; on by default.
props.label: A value shown above the end when the line arrives, in the accent. Optional.

moves.name: ring-sweep
moves.does: A ring fills clockwise from the top to its share of a whole.
moves.use_when: A share of a whole, with its number in the middle.
moves.avoid_when: More than one ring on screen, and shares that need comparing with each other.

props.share: How much of the ring fills, 0 to 1.
props.out: Seconds when it leaves. Optional. The exit is shorter than the entry.
props.size: Diameter as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.weight: Thickness as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.over: How long it sweeps: a timing token. Optional; scene by default.
props.children: What sits in the middle, such as a Count with the same start. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: camera
moves.does: A wrapper that moves a whole shot one way: a slow drift, a push in on a point, or a follow behind the pointer. A push closes in at one steady rate, by a constant factor.
moves.use_when: Going from the whole window to the one element the beat is about, or keeping a held shot alive with a drift.
moves.avoid_when: More than one move in a shot (never in, out, in), and slow moves across small text.

props.children: The content of the shot. Keep the Stage outside it.
props.direction: For a drift: "in", "out", "up", "down", "left" or "right". Optional; in by default. Its size comes from the preset.
props.to: For a push or a follow: the point to go to, in pixels of the frame.
props.at: For a push: seconds when it starts. For a follow: seconds when the pointer clicks, which is when the camera lands.
props.scale: How far it zooms. Optional; at most 2.5.
props.over: For a push: "scene" or "hero". Optional; scene by default.

moves.technique_note: The follow move is technique 7, cursor lead; cursor-lead is that move with its cursor. Drift and push are moves inside a shot, not scene changes.

moves.name: container-transform
moves.does: A small card grows to become the whole frame, its content appearing in the last third; reversed, the frame shrinks back into the card.
moves.use_when: Going into a detail, or back out to the bigger picture.
moves.avoid_when: Twice in a row, and when the card and the next scene are on the same page colour as the stage.

props.children: The full-frame scene inside the container.
props.from: Where the small card sits: x, y, width and height in pixels of the frame.
props.at: Seconds when it starts to grow (or to shrink).
props.page: The brand page the container is painted in: "light" or "dark".
props.card: What the small card shows, such as a label. Optional.
props.reverse: Start full and shrink to the card. Optional.
props.radius: Corner radius of the card as a percentage of frame height. Optional.

moves.name: push-through
moves.does: The camera pushes into one element until its colour fills the frame, and that colour is the page of the next scene. What grows is a plain plate over the element; the rest of the outgoing scene softens and is gone before it is enlarged, and the next scene starts on the frame after the colour covers the frame.
moves.use_when: Entering a new world: product to brand, light to dark.
moves.avoid_when: The element has fine detail, or the two scenes are on the same page.

props.children: The outgoing scene, with the element in it.
props.next: The next scene. Its clock starts at 0 on the frame after the colour covers the frame.
props.target: The element to enter: x, y, width and height in pixels of the frame.
props.page: The brand page of the element and of the next scene: "light" or "dark".
props.radius: Corner radius of the element as a percentage of frame height. Optional; the brand's control radius by default.

moves.planned_note: At 2.45 s the plate hands over to the page it has become; the picture does not change on that frame.

moves.name: relay-scroll
moves.does: The outgoing content speeds up and off, blurring along its way, is swapped in one frame, and the incoming content starts a little low and slows to rest. No fade, and no empty page between.
moves.use_when: Moving to the next step in a sequence.
moves.avoid_when: Unrelated scenes, and changing direction between steps of one film.

props.next: The incoming content. Its clock starts at 0 on the swap; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing content starts to leave.
props.reach: How far the outgoing content must travel to be out of the frame, as a share of the frame: 1 for content that fills it, about 0.6 for a line or a card in the middle. Optional; 1 by default.

moves.name: zoom-through-swap
moves.does: The outgoing group shrinks, speeding up, and dissolves over one tick into the next, which is already shrinking from large and slows to its size. It reads as one pull-back; there is no empty frame.
moves.use_when: A full change of content inside one world.
moves.avoid_when: Text that must be read during the swap, and next to another zoom.

props.next: The incoming group. Its clock starts at 0 as it appears, half a tick before the middle of the join; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing group starts to shrink.

moves.planned_note: The join at 2.11 s is a dissolve one tick long, not an instant change.

moves.name: slide-off-reveal
moves.does: Finished content speeds up and off one side, blurring along its way, while the next title, already beneath it, comes up.
moves.use_when: Ending a section and naming the next.
moves.avoid_when: The middle of a section, and when the next thing is not a title.

props.next: The title beneath. Give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the content starts to leave.

moves.name: light-sweep
moves.does: One soft band of light crosses a surface once. The band carries a faint wash of the accent, so it also shows on near-white cards.
moves.use_when: A reveal: the moment a result or a new state appears.
moves.avoid_when: More than once in a film, and on a loop.

props.children: The surface: a card, a window or a button.
props.at: Seconds when the band starts to cross.
props.radius: Corner radius of the surface as a percentage of frame height. Optional.
props.style: Extra CSS for placing it. Optional.

moves.name: parallax-camera
moves.does: Three planes at different depths slide at different speeds as the camera moves: the far plane 35% as far as the product and out of focus, the near plane 150% as far.
moves.use_when: A camera move that should feel like a space: arriving at a product screen, or travelling across a workspace.
moves.avoid_when: The near plane would cross what is being read, and shots with nothing behind or in front of the product.

props.children: The product plane, laid out as it should be when the camera has arrived.
props.far: What sits far behind it, softened and dimmed. Optional.
props.near: A foreground detail in front of it. Optional. Keep it clear of what is read.
props.at: Seconds when the camera starts to move.
props.by: How far the product plane slides, as shares of the frame's width and height (x and y). The camera moves the other way.

moves.name: momentum-cut
moves.does: The outgoing shot starts to slide, speeding up; a hard cut; the incoming shot is already moving the same way, at the same speed, and settles in about 300 ms.
moves.use_when: Joining two zoom levels of the same screen (the whole view, then one element close up) without zooming across small text.
moves.avoid_when: The two shots are on different pages or in different worlds, and calm passages where a carried move would do.

props.next: The incoming shot. Its clock starts at 0 on the cut; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing shot starts to move. The cut is one quick length later.

moves.name: shared-element
moves.does: One element travels on a shallow arc from its place in one layout to its place in the next, changing size and corner radius. Its place sets off first and its size lands last; its text changes over only at the midpoint and is never stretched.
moves.use_when: Two layouts share one thing: a row that becomes a card, a button that becomes a header. The default way to change scene inside a product.
moves.avoid_when: The two layouts share nothing, and more than one shared element at a time.

props.from: Where the element is in the first layout: x, y, width and height in pixels of the frame.
props.to: Where it is in the second layout.
props.at: Seconds when it sets off. The move takes a base and a tick.
props.before: What it holds in the first layout, laid out at that size. Optional.
props.after: What it holds in the second layout, laid out at that size. Optional.
props.radius: Corner radius before and after, as percentages of frame height. Optional; the brand's control and window radii by default.
props.style: Extra CSS for the surface. Optional.

moves.name: cursor-lead
moves.does: A large cursor travels on an arc and clicks; the camera sets off a quick length after it, covers 70% of the way while pushing in, and lands with the click. Pressed, exported beside it, dips the control under the click.
moves.use_when: Tutorials and demos: the next thing happens where the cursor goes.
moves.avoid_when: No interaction is happening, and anything on screen that changes before the click.

props.children: The screen. Put the clicked control in a Pressed with the same at.
props.from: Where the cursor starts, in pixels of the frame.
props.to: The point it clicks, in pixels of the frame.
props.at: Seconds when it clicks, which is when the camera lands. Show the result one frame later.
props.scale: How far the camera pushes in. Optional.
props.bend: How far the cursor's path bows, as a share of the distance. Optional.
props.out: Seconds when the cursor leaves. Optional.

moves.name: icon-door
moves.does: An icon tile sits in front of a miniature of a live screen. The camera pushes through in about 600 ms as the tile slides away, and the miniature is the screen; run back, in about 850 ms, the screen shrinks to a card and the tile slides back over it.
moves.use_when: Entering and leaving an app or a feature from a menu, a hub or a dashboard.
moves.avoid_when: Any other meaning in the same film, and a screen that cannot be shown small without looking broken.

props.children: The screen behind the door, laid out at full size. Its clock starts at 0 on at, so it builds while the camera travels.
props.icon: What the tile shows, in the middle of it.
props.tile: Where the tile sits: x, y, width and height in pixels of the frame.
props.at: Seconds when the camera starts through.
props.back: Seconds when it comes back out. Optional.
props.around: The rest of the menu. It goes as the camera passes and returns on the way back. Optional.
props.page: The brand page of the screen, if it is not the page the menu is on. Optional.

moves.name: cursor-classic
moves.does: A clean, generic arrow with a soft shadow, about 1.5 times a real pointer, in the brand's pointer colours. It turns into a hand over buttons and a text bar over fields, and presses to 90% on each click.
moves.use_when: Most demos and tutorials.
moves.avoid_when: Films that want no pointer at all (use hidden).

moves.name: cursor-brand
moves.does: The same arrow filled with the brand's accent colour and a rounder, heavier outline.
moves.use_when: Branded launches and social cuts.
moves.avoid_when: Screens where the accent colour is everywhere already, so the pointer would get lost.

moves.name: cursor-dot
moves.does: A small solid dot with a light ring.
moves.use_when: Montages and calm films, where the pointer should hardly be noticed.
moves.avoid_when: Tutorials: a dot does not show where exactly the click lands.

moves.name: cursor-halo
moves.does: A small accent dot inside a soft ring of light.
moves.use_when: Dark product screens and dark stages.
moves.avoid_when: Light, busy screens, where the ring reads as a stain.

moves.name: cursor-spotlight
moves.does: The classic arrow lights a soft circle around itself while the rest of the screen dims slightly.
moves.use_when: Busy screens where the eye needs guiding.
moves.avoid_when: Shots where something else on the screen must be read, and together with a focus pull (one emphasis per beat).

moves.name: cursor-presenter
moves.does: A larger arrow with a bold outline that still reads on a phone.
moves.use_when: Social cuts and tutorials watched on phones.
moves.avoid_when: Wide desktop films, where it looks oversized.

moves.name: cursor-named
moves.does: An accent arrow with a name tag, as in shared editors.
moves.use_when: Two-person and collaboration moments.
moves.avoid_when: Films with one person: a name tag invents a second user.

props.cursorName: The name on the tag, made up and safe to show.

moves.name: cursor-touch
moves.does: A soft see-through dot that presses down, with a ring on each tap and a short fading line while dragging.
moves.use_when: Phone-sized takes.
moves.avoid_when: Desktop takes: there is no finger on a desktop.

moves.name: cursor-hidden
moves.does: No pointer; the camera and the click effects lead.
moves.use_when: Cinematic shots and hero moments.
moves.avoid_when: Tutorials: people need to see where to click.

moves.name: click-ring
moves.does: A thin accent ring spreads from the click point and fades, starting as the button goes down.
moves.use_when: Most films: the default click.
moves.avoid_when: More than one click effect in a film.

moves.name: click-pulse
moves.does: A soft accent fill pulses over the button that was clicked (its tracked box), or a soft disc where nothing is tracked.
moves.use_when: Launches and demos where the button itself is the point.
moves.avoid_when: Small icons and dense rows, where the fill covers the neighbours.

moves.name: click-burst
moves.does: Eight short accent lines burst out from the click and fade. In a film that is not hype it becomes a ring.
moves.use_when: Hype films and social cuts.
moves.avoid_when: Calm and confident films.

moves.name: click-squish
moves.does: No mark on the screen: the pointer presses deeper (to 82%) and springs back.
moves.use_when: Films with sound on, where the click sound carries the moment.
moves.avoid_when: Sound-off social cuts: a squish alone is easy to miss.

moves.name: hover-magnet
moves.does: In the last fifth of a move the pointer is pulled onto its target a little faster, as if drawn in. The click still lands at the recorded place and time.
moves.use_when: Demos and launches.
moves.avoid_when: Calm and documentary films.

moves.name: hover-glow
moves.does: The tracked thing under a resting pointer gets a soft accent glow; it fades as the pointer moves on.
moves.use_when: Guiding the eye to the button about to be clicked.
moves.avoid_when: Untracked captures (nothing to glow), and beats that already carry another emphasis.

moves.name: typing-caret-glow
moves.does: The field being typed in glows with an accent edge that brightens on each key. The engine does not know the caret's exact place, so the whole field glows.
moves.use_when: Any typing worth watching.
moves.avoid_when: Pasted text that is not the point of the shot.

moves.name: typing-key-caps
moves.does: Shortcuts (or every key, in tutorials) show as key caps near the bottom of the screen; each cap presses as its key goes down.
moves.use_when: Shortcuts the viewer should learn.
moves.avoid_when: Ordinary typing: key caps for every letter are noise.

moves.name: camera-auto-zoom
moves.does: Before each action the camera eases in on the real thing it happens to (from tracks.json) with room around it, holds through the action and a proof moment, and eases out. Actions close in time and place share one shot. Never past 2x, never during a reading hold.
moves.use_when: Every demo: the default camera.
moves.avoid_when: Captures where the whole screen must stay in view, and documentary films.

moves.name: camera-follow
moves.does: While zoomed in, the camera drifts towards the pointer 150 ms behind it and covers 30% of the way, never so far that the thing leaves the shot.
moves.use_when: Demos with travel inside one zoomed area.
moves.avoid_when: Tutorials, where a steady frame is easier to follow.

moves.name: camera-push-in
moves.does: A slow move in on a thing, a click or a box, by hand.
moves.use_when: Landing a proof moment.
moves.avoid_when: Pushing in, out and in again in one shot.

moves.name: camera-pull-out
moves.does: Starts close on a detail and reveals the whole screen.
moves.use_when: Opening a scene on the result, then showing where it lives.
moves.avoid_when: Text that is being read while the camera moves.

moves.name: camera-snap-zoom
moves.does: A fast zoom with a tiny settle, for beats. In a film that is not hype it is an ordinary push in.
moves.use_when: Hype films, on a beat.
moves.avoid_when: Calm and confident films.

moves.name: camera-dolly-tilt
moves.does: The screen starts turned in depth (at most 10 degrees) and straightens as the camera moves in a little. Turns fade away as the camera closes in: wides only.
moves.use_when: Openings and wide establishing shots.
moves.avoid_when: Any screen that must be read while it is turned.

moves.name: camera-float
moves.does: The screen drifts very slowly in depth (about 2 degrees), alive through holds. Wides only.
moves.use_when: Launch hero shots and long holds on a wide screen.
moves.avoid_when: Tutorials and zoomed shots.

moves.name: camera-crane-reveal
moves.does: Starts tight on one thing and rises to the whole page, leaning back a little in depth on the way.
moves.use_when: Revealing the whole product after a detail.
moves.avoid_when: Short shots: it needs a hero length.

moves.name: camera-orbit
moves.does: A small turn around the floating screen, from one side to the other (at most 10 degrees). Wides only.
moves.use_when: Launch hero shots.
moves.avoid_when: Anything that must be read.

moves.name: camera-rack-focus
moves.does: One thing is sharp and the rest softens and dims; the sharp area moves to a second thing.
moves.use_when: Moving the eye from a cause to its result on one screen.
moves.avoid_when: Together with a spotlight pointer (one emphasis per beat).

moves.name: camera-pan-across
moves.does: A smooth slide across the screen at a set zoom, from one thing to another.
moves.use_when: Showing a long row of things, or two related places on one screen.
moves.avoid_when: Fast films: it needs a hero length.

moves.name: time-speed-ramp
moves.does: A long real wait (marked by the capture tool) or long typing plays faster, easing into and out of the faster speed, with a "Sped up" label in the brand's label style. The pointer, the tracked things and the camera follow the same clock.
moves.use_when: Any real wait over 0.6 s, and long typing.
moves.avoid_when: Waits that are the point of the story (show them, or cut them with a jump).

moves.name: time-freeze
moves.does: One moment of the recording holds while the camera pushes in slowly (5%), then eases back as the picture plays on.
moves.use_when: Proof moments: a result the viewer should believe.
moves.avoid_when: More than once or twice a film.

moves.name: time-jump
moves.does: A dead stretch is left out with a clean cut.
moves.use_when: Long waits where nothing changes on screen.
moves.avoid_when: Stretches where the pointer or the page is moving (the cut would show).

moves.name: time-rewind
moves.does: The recording runs backwards for a moment, easing in and out, then plays on from there or cuts back to where it was.
moves.use_when: Undo stories and "let us see that again".
moves.avoid_when: More than once a film.

moves.name: time-pin
moves.does: An event (a click, a mark, a step) lands on a chosen film time, such as a word of the voice. The pauses between actions are stretched or squeezed to fit; actions are never retimed.
moves.use_when: Fitting a capture to the voice.
moves.avoid_when: Pins that need the pauses to play more than 8 times faster or 4 times slower (the engine refuses, with a plain message).

moves.name: time-loop
moves.does: In its last stretch the clip dissolves back to its first frame while the camera and the pointer go back, so it can play in a loop.
moves.use_when: Social loops and website heroes.
moves.avoid_when: Films that end on a call to action.

moves.does: Every letter is a drum that rolls up through the alphabet and stops on its own letter, one after another; blurred while it spins, sharp when it stops.
moves.use_when: A name or a word that is dialled in; games, offers, reveals.
moves.avoid_when: Long lines; text that must stay readable throughout.

props.lines: film type
props.out: seconds, optional

sound.note: A ratchet that slows into each stop.

moves.planned_note: Flashes: up to 9 flashes a second over about 4% of the frame, within the limit (25% of the frame).

moves.name: pixel-decode
moves.does: A line resolves from coarse blocks to sharp type in six steps, as an image does when it loads. An SVG filter on the real text, so it needs no canvas.
moves.use_when: A digital reveal that does not move; data and image products.
moves.avoid_when: Small type (the first steps hide most of the line); more than three lines.

props.lines: film type, a line after the first starts a little later
props.out: seconds, optional

sound.note: Six quick steps can take a short rising chirp.

moves.planned_note: Each of the six block sizes appears as an instant change, about 0.15 s apart from 0.4 s; the second line steps about 0.13 s later.

moves.name: glitch-in
moves.does: The line arrives through six steps of digital glitch: a few bands slide sideways and a thin split in the accent and second colours, then it settles clean; the exit glitches for three steps and fades.
moves.use_when: A hard, techy opening; breaking-news or error-themed lines.
moves.avoid_when: Calm or luxury brands; anyone sensitive to flicker.

props.lines: film type
props.out: seconds, optional

sound.note: A short glitch burst; another on the exit.

moves.planned_note: Flash safety: the type never changes brightness or opacity while glitching; only bands of the line (never the full frame) move sideways and a thin colour fringe shows. Each step is an instant change about 0.06 s apart.
moves.house_rule: Banned by default in knowledge/craft/03-transitions.md (the template-pack glitch look). Use only with the owner's yes for this film, recorded in job.json.

moves.name: anagram
moves.does: The letters of a line shuffle into place: from a shuffled order (or from another phrase made of the same letters) each letter travels on its own arc to its spot, with motion blur while it travels.
moves.use_when: A reveal of the real line; wordplay; 'sort out the mess' stories.
moves.avoid_when: Long lines; more than one line; starred words (not supported).

props.from: optional start phrase with the same letters; otherwise a seeded shuffle
props.out: seconds, optional

sound.note: A soft sweep as the letters travel.

moves.name: highlighter
moves.does: A soft accent marker sweeps behind the chosen words, with a slightly uneven, seeded edge; the ink stays on top.
moves.use_when: The phrase that carries the offer or the benefit.
moves.avoid_when: Dark pages with a very light accent, where the marker is lost; more than one phrase in a beat.

moves.use_when: A word that wants attention without a colour change.
moves.avoid_when: Non-variable headline faces (falls back to opacity and scale); narrow frames with a long word, where the width changes show.

moves.name: letter-wave
moves.does: The letters of the chosen word rise and fall once, one after another: a small nudge.
moves.use_when: A word to flag lightly, such as a speed claim.
moves.avoid_when: More than once in a beat; when nothing may move.

props.lines: The line, drawn by the move; star a word for the accent voice.
props.out: Seconds when the emphasis ends (the line stays; the scene takes the line away).

moves.name: voice-swap
moves.does: A word crossfades from the headline voice to the accent voice with a little blur while its slot resizes and the line re-flows smoothly.
moves.use_when: The word a sentence turns on, in a brand with an accent face.
moves.avoid_when: Brands with no accent face, where the swap is only a weight change.

props.lines: The line, drawn by the move; star a word for the accent voice.
props.out: Seconds when the emphasis ends (the line stays; the scene takes the line away).

moves.name: caption-box
moves.does: Short-form caption style: the spoken phrase in large type with a highlight box in the brand's caption highlight colour that slides from word to word as each is spoken. Words not yet spoken sit faint and come up as they are spoken.
moves.use_when: A brand that has chosen this style for 9:16 (or 4:5, 1:1) talking-head or voice-over film.
moves.avoid_when: Long phrases, wide films that already have the fixed glass caption, or any shot where the band is needed for product UI.

props.out: seconds when captions go
props.size: Type size, per cent of frame height. Default 8, capped at an eighth of the caption band's width.

moves.name: caption-pop
moves.does: Short-form caption style: the phrase in large type and the word being spoken swells and turns the highlight colour, popping slightly as it starts. Words not yet spoken sit faint and come up as they are spoken.
moves.use_when: A brand that has chosen this style for 9:16 film with fast, energetic speech.
moves.avoid_when: Calm or formal films; long words that crowd the line.

props.words: { text, start, end }[] in seconds on the scene clock
props.out: seconds when captions go
props.size: per cent of frame height

moves.name: one-word-stack
moves.does: A sentence shown one very large word at a time, each word replacing the last on its cue.
moves.use_when: A short punchy line (up to about seven words) that should hit like a beat: hooks, price drops.
moves.avoid_when: Anything the viewer has to read as a sentence at once.

props.at: seconds when the first word starts
props.times: optional start second of each word

moves.name: recentre-build
moves.does: Words are added one by one to a centred line, and the line glides to stay centred as each arrives.
moves.use_when: A statement built up to its last word; lists written as a sentence.
moves.avoid_when: Long sentences that already fill the width; text that must be read from the first frame.

props.at: seconds when the first word starts
props.pace: seconds between words (default three quarters of a base length)
props.out: seconds when it leaves
props.size: per cent of frame height, default 8

moves.name: make-room
moves.does: A word is put into a line that is already there; its neighbours slide apart to make room while it rises in.
moves.use_when: Adding the key word to a known line (a number, a promise): 'Your team ships twice as fast'.
moves.avoid_when: Lines where the word's place is not clear; a word that is not the one thing to look at.

props.out: seconds when it leaves
props.size: per cent of frame height, default 8

moves.name: ticker
moves.does: A band of repeating text scrolling across the frame in a seamless loop, one row per line, rows in opposite directions, on brand bands if wanted.
moves.use_when: Headers such as a launch day or sale band; a running strip at the top of a film.
moves.avoid_when: Anything that has to be read once; stars and dots are not used.

props.lines: one line per row (the text that repeats); stars ignored
props.out: seconds when it closes
props.size: per cent of frame height, default 6
props.band: true (default): rows on accent then ink bands; false: bare type
props.gap: space between repeats in em, default 1.4 (spaces only, no dots)
props.top: pixel top of the first row (default centred)

moves.name: on-path
moves.does: Text set along a gentle curve that draws on along the path; the curve is built from the frame's size.
moves.use_when: Seals, stamps and flourishes: 'Made by hand in Lisbon'.
moves.avoid_when: Long sentences; headlines that must be read fast.

props.out: seconds when it erases
props.size: per cent of frame height, default 7 (shrinks to fit the curve)
props.bend: rise of the curve as a share of frame width, default 0.09

sound.note: A soft swish that follows the draw.

moves.name: text-window
moves.does: Huge type used as a window: the letters are cut out of a brand-coloured page so the picture behind shows only through them; then the window can open until the picture fills the frame.
moves.use_when: Titles over a product shot or gradient; an opening that reveals the product.
moves.avoid_when: Thin typefaces or long words; where the picture behind is dull or low contrast.

props.lines: one to three short words; stars ignored
props.at: seconds when the cover fades in
props.open: seconds when the letters start to grow (optional)
props.focus: which letter of the first line the zoom centres on, default the middle one
props.out: seconds when the cover fades
props.size: per cent of frame height, default 24

sound.note: A rising whoosh as the window opens; none if it only holds.

moves.name: word-morph
moves.does: One word changes into another in the same place: the old blurs and shrinks out while the new blurs in, overlapping, and the width animates between them.
moves.use_when: Before and after in one line: 'Reports in seconds' to 'minutes'.
moves.avoid_when: More than two or three swaps in one shot.

props.lines: the words in order; the first appears on at; *word* in the accent voice
props.after: fixed text after the word (include its space)
props.at: seconds when the first word arrives
props.swaps: seconds of each swap, default every 1.4 s
props.out: seconds when it leaves
props.size: per cent of frame height, default 9

sound.note: One soft pop at each swap.

moves.name: exit-set
moves.does: Text already on screen leaves in a chosen way: drop, mask-fall, blur-out, scatter, letter-fade or wipe. Each exit is shorter than an entry and speeds up.
moves.use_when: Clearing a line before the next one; matching the leave to the beat.
moves.avoid_when: Text that should stay; several different exits in one scene.

props.lines: the text
props.kind: drop | mask-fall | blur-out | scatter | letter-fade | wipe
props.out: seconds when the exit starts
props.size: per cent of frame height, default 8

sound.note: A short swish on out.

moves.name: push-wipe
moves.does: The incoming scene pushes the outgoing one off the frame, both moving together, hard and fast with motion blur. Never an empty frame.
moves.use_when: A firm change of subject on a beat; energy 3 to 5.
moves.avoid_when: Calm films; text that must be read in the first 0.3 s after the push.

moves.name: feather-wipe

moves.use_when: A gentle before-to-after reveal.
moves.avoid_when: A hard beat; a busy scene on both sides (the soft edge shows both at once).

props.next: the incoming scene; its clock starts at 0 when it takes over (the move does the wrapping)
props.page: stage name of the incoming scene's page (light or dark) when it is on the brand's other page

props.page: stage name of the incoming scene's page (light or dark) when it is on the brand's other page

sound.note: Short rising swell, no impact.

moves.avoid_when: Fast films; anything over a proof moment.

moves.name: door-split
moves.does: The outgoing scene splits in the middle and its halves slide apart, like doors, with the next scene behind and a soft shade at each edge.
moves.use_when: Opening on something: a reveal or launch.
moves.avoid_when: Outgoing scenes with fine detail across the middle seam.

props.next: the incoming scene; its clock starts at 0 when it takes over (the move does the wrapping)
props.page: stage name of the incoming scene's page (light or dark) when it is on the brand's other page

moves.does: The next scene is revealed through slices that open one after another from their middles, like venetian blinds.

moves.avoid_when: Most films: the craft file lists slat and blind wipes as generic; use once, where the rhythm is the point.

props.direction: left | right | up | down: where the opening starts and runs (default right)

sound.note: A quick stepped swish, one pulse per slice or one continuous swish.

moves.house_rule: Banned by default in knowledge/craft/03-transitions.md (slat and blind wipes). Use only with the owner's yes for this film, recorded in job.json.

moves.name: panel-wipe
moves.does: A solid accent panel sweeps across and covers the frame for a few frames; the next scene is there as it leaves. With trail, a panel in the incoming page's colour follows (accent, then the page).
moves.use_when: A strong change of chapter on a beat.
moves.avoid_when: Calm films; two panel wipes in one film.

props.page: stage name of the incoming scene's page (light or dark) when it is on the brand's other page
props.side: the side it travels towards (default right)

moves.name: dip-to-colour
moves.does: The scene dips into the brand's accent or page colour (never black), holds a few frames, and comes out in the next scene. No sound by default; a soft swell can sit under the dip.
moves.use_when: A quiet change of subject where nothing is near enough to carry the eye.
moves.avoid_when: When a hand-off object or a camera move can carry the change instead (the craft file's first choice).

props.next: the incoming scene; its clock starts at 0 when it takes over (the move does the wrapping)
props.page: stage name of the incoming scene's page (light or dark) when it is on the brand's other page
props.colour: accent | page (default accent): taken from the incoming page

moves.planned_note: The scenes swap on frame 148 (2.467 s) in the middle of the full-colour hold, so the change is hidden.

moves.name: blur-through
moves.does: The outgoing scene blurs and grows slightly as it leaves; the incoming scene is as blurred on the swap, then sharpens and settles. They cross over a single tick at the peak of the blur, so the frame is never empty.
moves.use_when: A soft change of thought inside one world: a headline into the product card, one panel into the next.
moves.avoid_when: Anything that must be read within 0.7 s of the change; very sharp, graphic, hype passages.

props.next: The incoming scene. Its clock starts at 0 as it takes over; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing scene starts to leave.

moves.planned_note: The swap, in the middle of the one-tick overlap of the two scenes, hidden by the blur or bloom at peak. Smoothness found no unplanned jumps and no judder; flashes passed.

moves.name: exposure-bloom
moves.does: The frame over-exposes into a bloom of the brand's lighter ink (brighter, softer, a little larger), the swap is hidden at the peak, and the bloom falls away on the next scene. One rise and one fall, about 0.8 s; the bloom is weaker at the corners, so the frame is never one flat white. Flash-safe.
moves.use_when: A reveal or a change of mood: before into after, problem into answer.
moves.avoid_when: More than once in a film (it is a flash); a light page where the brand's light ink is the page itself (the effect is faint there); photosensitive audiences should still be tested for broadcast.

props.next: The incoming scene. Its clock starts at 0 as it takes over; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing scene starts to leave.

sound.note: A short bright riser that peaks on the swap and resolves into a soft tail; one sound, not a riser and a hit.

moves.planned_note: The swap, in the middle of the one-tick overlap of the two scenes, hidden by the blur or bloom at peak. Smoothness found no unplanned jumps and no judder; flashes passed.

moves.name: invert-flash
moves.does: A small push in, then on the cut the whole frame (page included) is inverted for exactly two frames, the last frame of the old scene and the first of the new, and the new scene settles. One frame-pair, once. Flash-safe: a single inversion, never repeated within a second.
moves.use_when: A hard beat in a hype film, on a downbeat.
moves.avoid_when: Calm films; text that needs reading in the 0.3 s around the cut; any second flash within a second of it.

props.next: The incoming scene. Its clock starts at 0 as it takes over; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing scene starts to leave.

sound.note: A short riser leads in over the push and a hard hit lands on the two inverted frames. Flash-safe: one inversion of two frames, no repeat.

moves.credit: After the camera transitions catalogued in Leonxlnx/cinetic (MIT); rebuilt for the studio's engine, no code copied
moves.planned_note: The cut under the two inverted frames (the inversion is the one planned flash: 0.97 to 0 and back, a single pair). Smoothness: no unplanned jumps, no judder. Flashes: pass, at most 1 flash a second.

moves.name: whip-pan
moves.does: Both scenes travel sideways at whip speed with strong directional blur; the swap is at peak speed, the incoming scene already moving the same way and slowing into place. The camera never stops between them.
moves.use_when: A quick change of place in a fast film: a number into its chart, one screen into another.
moves.avoid_when: Calm films, and any text that must be read within 0.7 s of the change. Once or twice a film (technique 11).

props.next: The incoming scene. Its clock starts at 0 as it takes over; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing scene starts to leave.

sound.note: A fast whoosh starting about 150 ms before the swap, peaking on it, with a short tail that matches the settle.

moves.credit: After the camera transitions catalogued in Leonxlnx/cinetic (MIT); rebuilt for the studio's engine, no code copied
moves.planned_note: The swap, in the middle of the one-tick overlap of the two scenes, hidden by the blur or bloom at peak. Smoothness found no unplanned jumps and no judder; flashes passed.

moves.name: zoom-blur
moves.does: A radial zoom blur: the outgoing scene rushes at the camera, smeared outwards from the centre (a trail of scaled copies with falling opacity); the incoming scene rushes out of the centre from small and settles at its own size.
moves.use_when: A hype change, or when the next thing is the thing to see: a headline into a number.
moves.avoid_when: Calm films; busy outgoing scenes (the trail muddies them); text near the edges of the outgoing scene.

props.next: The incoming scene. Its clock starts at 0 as it takes over; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing scene starts to leave.

sound.note: A rising whoosh that peaks on the swap and opens into a wide short tail.

moves.credit: After the camera transitions catalogued in Leonxlnx/cinetic (MIT); rebuilt for the studio's engine, no code copied
moves.planned_note: The swap, in the middle of the one-tick overlap of the two scenes, hidden by the blur or bloom at peak. Smoothness found no unplanned jumps and no judder; flashes passed.

moves.name: spin-whip
moves.does: A quick clockwise rotation about the middle of the frame with rotational blur (a trail of turned copies); the swap is at peak spin, the incoming scene already turning the same way from a quarter turn back and settling upright.
moves.use_when: A playful or hype change, once at most per film.
moves.avoid_when: Calm or serious films; scenes with a lot of fine text.

props.next: The incoming scene. Its clock starts at 0 as it takes over; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing scene starts to leave.

sound.note: A tight swish with a turning pitch, starting about 150 ms before the swap and peaking on it.

moves.credit: After the camera transitions catalogued in Leonxlnx/cinetic (MIT); rebuilt for the studio's engine, no code copied
moves.planned_note: The swap, in the middle of the one-tick overlap of the two scenes, hidden by the blur or bloom at peak. Smoothness found no unplanned jumps and no judder; flashes passed.

moves.name: parallax-push
moves.does: The outgoing scene's layers slide away at different speeds, the front fastest and the back slowest, as the next scene pushes in over them at the front layer's speed. Each side is blurred by its own speed.
moves.use_when: A change of place that should feel like depth, not a flat slide: when the outgoing scene has a background, a main layer and a foreground.
moves.avoid_when: A scene with only one layer (use whip-pan); calm passages that want a camera carry.

props.next: The incoming scene. Its clock starts at 0 as it takes over; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing scene starts to leave.
props.layers: The outgoing scene as an array of layers, back to front. Or give `background` and the `children` as the foreground.
props.background: The back layer, with `children` as the foreground.

sound.note: A soft wide whoosh, starting about 150 ms before the swap, peaking on it with a long tail as the layers settle.

moves.credit: After the camera transitions catalogued in Leonxlnx/cinetic (MIT); rebuilt for the studio's engine, no code copied
moves.planned_note: The swap, in the middle of the one-tick overlap of the two scenes, hidden by the blur or bloom at peak. Smoothness found no unplanned jumps and no judder; flashes passed.

moves.name: match-cut
moves.does: A shape in the outgoing scene and one in the incoming scene occupy exactly the same place on the cut: the outgoing scene eases its scale and place so its shape lands on a common rectangle on the last frame before the cut, the incoming scene starts with its shape on that same rectangle and eases to rest, and the common rectangle is chosen so both move at the same speed.
moves.use_when: A strong beat where two scenes share a shape (a button into a chart ring, a dot into a big disc), energy 4 to 5. Technique 5.
moves.avoid_when: Shapes that differ in size by more than about a quarter of the frame, or in proportions (the match is then only of centre and area).

props.next: The incoming scene. Its clock starts at 0 as it takes over; give it no entrance of its own.
props.at: Seconds when the outgoing scene starts to leave.
props.from: Rect in pixels of the frame: the shape in the outgoing scene (x, y, width, height).
props.to: Rect in pixels of the frame: the matching shape in the incoming scene.

sound.note: A quick swish into the cut and a soft low thud on the cut frame, where the two shapes line up.

moves.credit: After the camera transitions catalogued in Leonxlnx/cinetic (MIT); rebuilt for the studio's engine, no code copied
moves.planned_note: The swap, in the middle of the hard cut (one frame the old scene, the next the new). Smoothness found no unplanned jumps and no judder; flashes passed.

moves.name: cube-turn
moves.does: The two scenes are two faces of one cube; the cube turns a quarter turn (a scene and a quick length, about 960 ms) to bring the next face round, the camera pulling back at the middle so the whole cube is seen. The face turning away darkens and the cube's edges are drawn while it turns. Both faces move on every frame of the turn, motion-blurred at its fastest. The faces are sheets painted exactly like the stage, so nothing changes on the page before or after.
moves.use_when: Stepping to a neighbouring item of one set: this feature, then the next; this month, then the next.
moves.avoid_when: The two scenes belong to different worlds, or a calm film where a 3D turn would be the loudest thing in it. Not twice in a row.

props.next: the incoming scene; its clock starts at 0 on `at`, when it starts to turn into view
props.to: left | right | up | down: the way the content moves (default left)

sound.note: Starts 150-200 ms before `at` and peaks at the middle of the turn (`at` + 0.48 s), where the turn is fastest.

moves.credit: Idea after gl-transitions "Cube" by gre (MIT, https://github.com/gl-transitions/gl-transitions); rebuilt for the studio's engine, no code copied
moves.swap: No cut. In the preview the next face turns into view from 1.50 s, is half way at 1.98 s and is alone from 2.46 s.

moves.name: card-flip
moves.does: The scene lifts off the page as a card with round corners and a shadow, flips over about its upright axis (or its level one with `over`) and the next scene is on its back; the card grows back to fill the frame. About 1.15 s. The swap is the frame on which the card is edge-on, half way, where it turns fastest, so both sides are moving and the swap is unseen.
moves.use_when: The other side of one thing: a question and its answer, before and after, a price and what it buys.
moves.avoid_when: The two scenes are not two sides of one idea; more than once in a film.

props.children: the front of the card (outgoing scene)
props.next: the back of the card; its clock starts at 0 on `at`
props.over: true to flip about the level axis, top towards the viewer (default false: about the upright axis)

sound.note: Peaks on the edge-on frame (`at` + 0.575 s); a soft tap as the card lands flat is optional.

moves.swap: In the preview the flip runs 1.60 s to 2.75 s; the faces swap on the edge-on frame at 2.175 s (frame 130-131 at 60 fps).

moves.name: page-turn
moves.does: The scene is a page: its right edge lifts and curls over a moving upright fold, the turned-over part (plain back of the page) lies on top and leaves to the left, showing the next page beneath with the fold's shadow on it. The next page settles from slightly larger. About 1.15 s. Built from thin strips of one sheet in CSS 3D, with the light changing smoothly across them; frame-pure, no pictures, no WebGL.
moves.use_when: The next chapter of a guide, a report, a story; a list of steps read like a booklet.
moves.avoid_when: Product UI that should feel live rather than printed; energy 5 films.

props.next: the page beneath; its clock starts at 0 on `at`

sound.note: One page-turn rustle starting just before `at`, its loudest part about 0.4 s in.

moves.swap: No cut: the next page is uncovered from the right edge from 1.50 s to 2.65 s in the preview.

moves.name: tile-reveal
moves.does: The frame becomes a grid of tiles (about five and a half on the short side, so a tall frame has more rows, not taller tiles); a wave runs diagonally from a corner and each tile turns over in a base length to show its piece of the next scene, dipping a little with round corners so the grid shows for a moment. About 1.15 s in all. The outgoing scene grows slightly and the next settles from slightly larger, so both move while tiles swap.
moves.use_when: A change of set: a new month, a new collection, a new board; a playful, organised film.
moves.avoid_when: A single object should carry the change (use a hand-off); calm films.

props.next: the incoming scene; its clock starts at 0 on `at`
props.from: top-left | top-right | bottom-left | bottom-right: the corner the wave starts from (default top-left)

sound.note: A light run of ticks or a granular sweep across the wave, `at` to `at` + 1.15 s; not one sound per tile.

moves.swap: Each tile swaps on its own edge-on frame; in the preview the first at about 1.80 s, the last at about 2.55 s; the wave runs 1.60 s to 2.75 s.

moves.name: pixelate-through
moves.does: The scene breaks into square blocks that grow (even in ratio) to about a ninth of the frame's short side, the blocks change from the outgoing scene's colours to the next's while biggest, and shrink until the next scene is sharp. About 960 ms. Drawn with an SVG filter on the live scenes (one pixel kept in the middle of each block, spread over it), not WebGL. Both scenes drift in scale through it. Flash check: at most 13 block changes in one second over 9.6% of the frame (limit 25%), passing.
moves.use_when: Digital, playful or retro films: a version change, a game-like reveal, an old screen to a new one.
moves.avoid_when: Premium or calm brands; anything where the blocks would read as a broken video.

props.next: the incoming scene; its clock starts at 0 on `at`
props.at: seconds when the blocks start to grow

sound.note: A soft bit-crush sweep up to the middle (`at` + 0.48 s) and down again; not a harsh glitch.

moves.credit: Idea after gl-transitions "Pixelize" by gre (MIT, https://github.com/gl-transitions/gl-transitions); rebuilt for the studio's engine, no code copied
moves.swap: In the preview the blocks run 1.50 s to 2.46 s; the scenes swap inside the blocks from 1.87 s to 2.10 s, while the blocks are biggest.

moves.name: luma-dissolve
moves.does: The next scene appears through soft-edged patches that grow and join like ink in water: a threshold sweeps through a fixed, seeded cloud of SVG noise, and the outgoing scene is cut by the same cloud the other way, so the two meet only in the soft edge. About 1.15 s. Patch size follows the frame's short side. Both scenes keep moving: the outgoing grows slightly, the incoming settles from slightly larger.
moves.use_when: A gentle change of time or mood ('later that day', 'by 5 pm'), in calm films.
moves.avoid_when: Between two worlds (the house rule bans crossfades there) or with dense small text on both sides at the same place.

props.next: the incoming scene; its clock starts at 0 on `at`
props.seed: which noise cloud (whole number, default 7): the same seed renders the same every time

sound.note: A soft airy swell starting just before `at`, peaking about `at` + 0.6 s.

moves.credit: Idea after gl-transitions "LumaWipe" by gre (MIT, https://github.com/gl-transitions/gl-transitions); rebuilt for the studio's engine, no code copied
moves.swap: No cut: patches of the next scene show from 1.50 s and the last pixels turn on 2.65 s in the preview.

moves.name: title-takeover
moves.does: One big word lands over the scene in the headline voice and ink (the scene shrinks back and fades a little); then its letters become windows onto the next scene while the frame outside them is shaded, and the word grows around one letter and fattens until the windows fill the frame. Landing a base length, opening and growing about 1.15 s. The frame-wide shade carries the stage grain, so this preview was encoded at --crf=25 to stay small.
moves.use_when: Naming the next section as you enter it: 'Reports', 'Pricing', 'Teams'. One short heavy word.
moves.avoid_when: Long words or two lines; a film that already uses a text window; more than once in a film.

props.next: the incoming scene; its clock starts at 0 when the letters open (`at` + base + tick)
props.at: seconds when the word starts to land
props.size: type size, per cent of frame height (default 24); shrunk to fit 86% of the width
props.focus: which letter the word grows around, counted from 0 (default the middle one)

sound.note: A low thump as the word lands at `at`, then a rising whoosh that peaks as the letters fill the frame (about `at` + 1.65 s).

moves.swap: No cut. In the preview the word lands from 1.40 s, the letters open at 1.90 s and the next scene fills the frame at 3.05 s.

moves.name: logo-mask-wipe
moves.does: The brand's mark opens in the middle of the frame as a window onto the next scene (the frame outside it shaded), then grows, even in ratio, until it covers the frame. The mark is the dark page's mark file used only as a shape. Opening a base length, growing about 1.15 s; in the last tick whatever is left of the outgoing scene in the mark's gaps fades, so nothing is cut on the last frame. The frame-wide shade carries the stage grain, so this preview was encoded at --crf=25 to stay small.
moves.use_when: The move into the closing frame (wordmark and call to action), or out of the opening one. Once per film.
moves.avoid_when: The brand's dark mark file is a filled tile or has no clear background (the window would be a square); mid-film. An ending onto the same page: the frame outside the mark is darkened and reads muddy (found in the proof film); use it onto the other page.

props.focus: { x, y }: the point of the mark it grows around, from its middle in mark heights (default its middle); should lie in a solid part of the mark

sound.note: Rises from `at` and peaks as the mark covers the frame (`at` + 1.65 s); the brand's sting can follow on the closing frame.

moves.swap: No cut. In the preview the mark opens at 1.50 s, grows from 2.00 s and covers the frame at 3.15 s.

moves.name: light-leak
moves.does: A warm wash of light, tinted toward the brand's accent, drifts across the frame; the scene changes at its peak, hidden inside the light.
moves.use_when: Use sparingly, once a film at most. A warm, human beat: a launch, a season, a memory.
moves.avoid_when: Use sparingly: a stylised look that draws attention to itself. Product UI, data, or anything cool and exact; a film that already used a stylised transition.

props.next: The incoming scene; its own clock starts at the swap: a `tick`-long dissolve, inside the wash, centred at half of three quarters of a `hero` length after `at`.
props.seed: changes the shape of the leak (default 4)

sound.note: A soft airy swell that peaks at the swap and falls away.

moves.credit: Drawn from gradients. @remotion/light-leaks (4.0.543) was checked and not used: its leak is fixed yellow and orange and cannot be tinted to a brand's accent.
moves.flash_check: flashes.py passes on the preview (at most one flash in any second, none over the area limit).

moves.name: glitch-cut
moves.does: For about a quarter of a second the picture tears into slices that slip sideways, with two brand-coloured ghosts and accent bars, and the scene is different when it settles.
moves.use_when: Use sparingly, once a film at most. A tech or gaming beat, a 'before and after' on something broken or fast.
moves.avoid_when: Use sparingly: a stylised look that draws attention to itself. Calm, premium or human subjects; text that must be read during the glitch; any film for viewers sensitive to flicker.

props.next: the incoming scene; its own clock starts at the cut, the third step of the burst (0.1 s after `at`)
props.nextPage: the page the next scene is on, for the ghosts' blending (default: the other page)

moves.flash_check: flashes.py passes on the preview (at most one flash in any second, none over the area limit).

moves.name: ripple
moves.does: A ripple spreads from a point; inside the wavefront the next scene is already there, and the ring bends the picture like water.
moves.use_when: Use sparingly, once a film at most. A tap, a drop, a payment going through: a moment that starts from one point.
moves.avoid_when: Use sparingly: a stylised look that draws attention to itself. Text that must stay readable across the ring; busy or detailed scenes.

props.next: the incoming scene; there is no single swap frame: it is on screen inside the ripple from `at`, with its own clock starting at `at`
props.origin: where the ripple starts, shares of the frame {x, y} (the middle by default)

moves.use_when: Use sparingly, once a film at most. Handmade, craft, editorial or story subjects.
moves.avoid_when: Use sparingly: a stylised look that draws attention to itself. Product UI, data, or a tight timeline.

moves.name: ugc-comment-reply
moves.does: The question card a UGC film answers: a comment (avatar, handle, heart count) drops in at the top under a "Replying to @handle" line, can take a like tap, shrinks up to the top as the answer lands, and leaves.
moves.use_when: A UGC hook that answers a comment ("Wait, how do you keep every lead in one place?"); the card is the question, the film is the answer.
moves.avoid_when: Films with no creator voice; brands that avoid imitating a social app; a real person's comment (write an original line, never quote a real one).

props.handle: the commenter's handle, with or without @
props.label: the line above the card (default "Replying to @handle"; "" for none)
props.likes: the number beside the heart (leave out for no heart)
props.preroll: seconds of the arrival already done at `at` (for a card part-way in on frame 0)
props.out: seconds when it leaves
props.dockAt: seconds when it shrinks up to dockY (the answer lands)
props.dockY: where the docked card sits, share of frame height
props.x / y: middle of the card, shares of the frame
props.size: comment size, per cent of the short side (5.6 tall, 4.6 wide)
props.fill / ink / accent: colours; the brand's stage by default (an inverse card)

review.about: Every move was watched frame by frame at 60 frames a second, fixed and rendered again before it was marked reviewed. "planned_instant_changes" lists, in seconds of the move's own preview, each change that is meant to happen in one frame (a cut or a swap), so tools/checks/smoothness.py can be given them with --planned-cuts and report only the unplanned ones.
review.known_limit: The browser places every line of text on a whole pixel from top to bottom. A slow vertical settle of text therefore ends in steps of one pixel at full size (two in half-size previews). Moves keep small overshoots off text for this reason.

shared.about: Helpers every move can use, exported from engine/src/kit/moves.
shared.MotionBlur: Wraps anything that moves fast and blurs it along its way, matched to its speed (half-frame shutter). Nothing blurs below reading speed. Give it x and y, the pixels travelled this frame.
shared.useTravel: Gives the pixels travelled this frame for any place written as a function of scene time.

capture.about: Entries in the capture families are settings of CaptureClip, not components of their own. Their previews play a stretch of a real capture chosen from its own events (engine/src/library/motion/capture.tsx); the compositions take a "capture" prop ("<job>/<id>", empty for the newest). Check them with tools/checks/capture_motion.mjs as well as tools/checks/smoothness.py.
capture.practice_page_note: Previews were rendered at half size from a practice capture whose search box opens and closes in one frame, with no animation of its own. Those one-frame changes are in the recording itself and are listed in planned_instant_changes (typing-key-caps, time-speed-ramp, time-jump); a preview made from another capture has other ones.
capture.staging_and_product: Stagings are CaptureShot (engine/src/kit/capture/staging.tsx), product animations are CaptureClip's emphasis (emphasis.tsx), glued through glue.ts. Their previews (engine/src/library/motion/product.tsx) take "capture", "second", "things" (fixed places for a take that tracked nothing), "roles" and "address". Rendered at half size 12 Nov 2026: Tulvo's boards take (with its cards given as things, measured from the marks) for most, a practice take where typing, a message, a scroll or a second take was needed. Check glue with tools/checks/capture_glue.mjs on a GlueProbe render; measure where the picture really scrolled first with tools/film/seen_scroll.mjs.
capture.transitions: Entries in the capture-transition family are CaptureJoin with one "transition" name.
